_comment: Combined demo dataset: normalized findings from the mock HackerTarget, Quantro, and local-check sources, before deduplication and scoring. Placeholder assets only. Try it with: webscan prioritize --input data/mock_results.json --example-config. Regenerate with scripts/build_mock_results.py.

findings.description: The page loads an old jQuery version that can run attacker-supplied script when untrusted HTML is inserted into the page.
Old jQuery versions mishandle HTML from untrusted sources.
Old jQuery versions allow modification of built-in object behavior.

findings.vulnerability_name: SQL injection in donation search form
findings.description: The search box passes what a visitor types directly into a database query, so a visitor could read donor records from the database.

findings.vulnerability_name: Reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) in campaign page
findings.description: The campaign page repeats part of the web address back to the visitor without cleaning it.
The site does not tell browsers to always use a secure connection.

findings.vulnerability_name: Administrator login does not require multi-factor authentication
findings.description: Administrator accounts can sign in with only a password.

findings.vulnerability_name: Default administrator credentials accepted on staging CMS
findings.description: The staging content management system still accepts the vendor's default administrator username and password.

findings.vulnerability_name: SMBv1 enabled: remote code execution (EternalBlue, MS17-010)
findings.description: The file server still accepts the outdated SMBv1 file sharing protocol and is missing the MS17-010 security update.

findings.vulnerability_name: Operating system is end of life and no longer supported
findings.description: The file server runs an operating system version that no longer receives security updates from the vendor.
The web server shows a list of every file in the uploads folder.
